title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: How to quickly check whether the user has write (Insert, Delete, and Modify) permission for the table in AL
summary: This post explains how to use the Record.WritePermission() method in AL to check whether a user has write permissions (Insert, Delete, Modify) for a table before executing operations, allowing developers to perform alternative actions based on permission levels instead of triggering errors.
key_points: WritePermission() method checks if a user can write to a table, including full and partial write permissions with security filters
Without Insert permission, New actions are grayed out; without Modify permission, card pages open in View mode only
Developers can use WritePermission() to perform different operations conditionally based on user permissions
Example uses WritePermission() to open Vendor Card for users with write access, Customer Card for others

quotes.text: Record.WritePermission() Method: Determines whether a user can write to a table.
quotes.why_it_matters: This is the core method that enables developers to check write permissions before executing operations

quotes.text: A write permission consists of Insert, Delete, and Modify permissions.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies what constitutes write permission, helping developers understand the scope of the check
